To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the genetic algorithm technique is a promising tool for identifying optimal watershed management strategies, 2) the implementation of the most selected BMPs in the watershed can improve stream health by 52%, 3) the implementation of BMPs in the lowest costing scenario can improve stream health in 36% of the stream length, and 4) the implementation of no tillage is one of the best BMPs in the Honeyoey Pine Watershed.
a genetic algorithm was used to design the watershed-scale management strategies that included no tillage as the most selected BMP for the Honeyoee Creek Pine Creek Watersheds in Michigan.
The integration of genetic algorithm and stream health modeling can be used to identify the optimal BMP implementation strategy that results in a desired stream health at the lowest cost.

the optimization of conservation practice implementation plans to improve stream health.
the design of a management plan for improving the overall stream health of a watershed by implementing the best management practices (BMPs).
improving stream health in the context of watershed scale BMP implementation.
